_instructions: Read the claim and the experiment, then fill expected_verdict with your own judgment: ACCURATE (conveys the correct thing) / MIXED (right idea, under-specified or missing a minor element) / IRRELEVANT (would not yield useful information about the claim). Leave items blank to skip them — label maybe 10, mixing obvious and subtle cases. The judge's verdicts are intentionally not shown here; run `python -m norm_cards.eval.calibrate` to compare.

items.claim:
An Ultralytics YOLO11n detector pretrained on COCO and evaluated on the person class of the COCO val2017 split at 640×640 resolution,retains AP50 ≥ 0.90 (IoU ≥ 0.5), with ≤ 5% relative degradation from clean performance under adversarial perturbations under image modifications under a learned generative illumination-consistent perturbation model. The image manipulations follow a white-box projected gradient descent (PGD) attack over the latent variables of the learned conditional generative model, with perturbations constrained to remain within an L∞ image-space bound of ε = 12/255.
Note that the conditional generator is learned from the COCO data set to describe the perturbation set over a constrained latent space of lighting parameters. The generator g(x,z) produces perturbed images (for original image x) where z lies in a norm-bounded latent space (e.g., \|z\| \le B ); g is a trained conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE).
items.experiment: To address subclaims 1–7, evaluate the exact released Ultralytics YOLO11n COCO-pretrained checkpoint, e.g. yolo11n.pt from the Ultralytics package/model hub, on the public COCO val2017 split using only category_id=1/person annotations and inference size imgsz=640. Use the standard COCO evaluation API or Ultralytics val mode, report class-wise AP50 at IoU=0.5 for person on clean images, and record the model identifier, checkpoint provenance, preprocessing, NMS settings, and resolution. If the checkpoint is not YOLO11n, is not COCO-pretrained, is not evaluated on COCO val2017/person, or the resolution/IoU metric differs, the corresponding setup subclaims fail. If clean person AP50 is below 0.90, the later robustness claim becomes unlikely or impossible to support as stated; if clean AP50 is only slightly above 0.90, the ≤5% degradation condition imposes a very tight attacked AP50 threshold. This experiment could be made unnecessary for the setup facts by official Ultralytics documentation and reproducible validation logs showing the same checkpoint, dataset, resolution, and class-wise AP50.

items.experiment: To address subclaims 8 and 12–16, train or obtain a conditional variational autoencoder on publicly available COCO train2017 images, conditioned on the original image x and a norm-bounded latent vector z intended to encode lighting parameters, then validate that g(x,z) outputs perturbed images that are illumination-consistent rather than arbitrary corruptions. Use held-out COCO val2017 images, sample z within the claimed bound ||z||≤B, and measure: reconstruction/ELBO quality, image-space L∞ distances, changes in luminance/chromaticity statistics, preservation of geometry/semantic content via segmentation or feature similarity, and whether traversals in z correspond primarily to lighting changes. If the CVAE cannot be trained to produce realistic illumination-consistent perturbations from COCO, or z is not norm-bounded/does not control lighting, the generative-perturbation-set subclaims are unsupported. If outputs are realistic, geometry-preserving, and controlled by bounded z, the generator assumptions become plausible for the attack experiment. This experiment could be reduced or skipped if the claimant provides the trained CVAE, architecture, training data split, latent-bound definition, and quantitative/qualitative validation of illumination consistency.

An Ultralytics YOLO11n detector pretrained on COCO and evaluated on the person class of the COCO val2017 split at 640×640 resolution,retains AP50 ≥ 0.90 (IoU ≥ 0.5), with ≤ 5% relative degradation from clean performance under adversarial perturbations under image modifications under a learned generative illumination-consistent perturbation model. The image manipulations follow a white-box projected gradient descent (PGD) attack over the latent variables of the learned conditional generative model, with perturbations constrained to remain within an L∞ image-space bound of ε = 12/255.

The generator g(x,z) produces perturbed images (for original image x) where z lies in a norm-bounded latent space (e.g., \|z\| \le B ); g is a trained conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE).
items.experiment: To address subclaims 5 and 7–11, perform the full white-box projected-gradient-descent attack over the CVAE latent variables against the YOLO11n detector, using COCO val2017/person at 640×640. For each image, optimize z by backpropagating through g(x,z) and the detector loss, projecting z into its norm bound after each step, while also enforcing or rejecting samples that violate the image-space L∞ constraint ||g(x,z)-x||∞≤12/255. Evaluate attacked images with COCO AP50 for the person class at IoU=0.5, and compute relative degradation = (clean AP50 − attacked AP50)/clean AP50. Include PGD hyperparameter sweeps, multiple random restarts, and sanity checks against non-generative L∞ PGD or random latent perturbations to verify the attack is meaningfully white-box and strong. If attacked AP50 remains ≥0.90 and relative degradation is ≤5% under a well-tuned attack, the central robustness claim is supported; if AP50 falls below 0.90 or degradation exceeds 5%, the claim fails; if stronger PGD settings continue to reduce AP, earlier results were attack-weakness artifacts. This experiment could be made unnecessary only by complete reproducible attack code, trained generator weights, exact PGD parameters, and independent logs showing the same constrained L∞ latent-PGD evaluation.

items.experiment: To address subclaim 1 (and subclaims 2–7), reproduce the clean COCO-val2017 person-class evaluation using the exact Ultralytics YOLO11n COCO-pretrained checkpoint. Download COCO val2017 and annotations from a public source such as HuggingFace/Kaggle/COCO, load the official Ultralytics YOLO11n pretrained weights, run inference with imgsz=640, and compute AP50 for category_id=1/person using pycocotools at IoU=0.5. Record the model name/checkpoint hash, whether the weights are COCO-pretrained, the image size, class filtering procedure, confidence/NMS settings, and clean person AP50. items.experiment: To address subclaim 8 (and subclaims 12–16), audit and reproduce the learned conditional generative illumination-consistent perturbation model. Train or obtain the claimed CVAE generator g(x,z) using COCO train2017 images, with x as the conditioning image and z as a norm-bounded lighting latent variable, then evaluate on held-out COCO val2017 images. Verify that g takes an original image x plus latent z and outputs a perturbed image, that z is explicitly projected or sampled within ||z||≤B, that the architecture is a trained conditional VAE, and that generated changes are illumination-like rather than arbitrary texture/object changes. Quantify this by measuring reconstruction/regularization losses, image-space L∞ distances, color/brightness/shading statistics, and perceptual or semantic consistency using public models; visually inspect random samples and latent traversals. If the generator produces only smooth lighting/color changes while preserving scene geometry and object identity, the generative-illumination subclaims are plausible. If it introduces object distortions, non-lighting artifacts, or lacks a bounded latent space, those subclaims are unsupported and the adversarial robustness result would not test the stated threat model. This experiment could be made unnecessary by a released trained CVAE checkpoint, architecture, training data split, latent-bound definition, and sample outputs demonstrating illumination consistency.

items.experiment: To address subclaim 9 (and subclaims 5, 7, 10, and 11), run the actual white-box PGD attack over the CVAE latent variables and evaluate robust person AP50 on COCO val2017. Use the differentiable YOLO11n detection loss with full access to model weights, backpropagate through g(x,z), update z by PGD with multiple restarts, project z back into its norm-bounded latent set, and additionally reject or project outputs so that ||g(x,z)-x||∞≤12/255 in normalized image space. Evaluate the attacked images at 640×640 with pycocotools AP50 for the person class and compute relative degradation: (clean AP50 − adversarial AP50)/clean AP50. Include attack-strength checks such as increasing PGD steps/restarts, comparing against random latent perturbations, and confirming that gradients are nonzero and the attack reduces detector confidence/localization. If adversarial AP50 remains ≥0.90 and relative degradation is ≤5% under the strongest white-box latent PGD tested, the main robustness claim is supported. If AP50 falls below 0.90 or degradation exceeds 5%, the claim is refuted for this implementation. If weak PGD fails but stronger PGD succeeds, the original attack was insufficient. This experiment could be made unnecessary by released adversarial images, attack code, hyperparameters, model/generator checkpoints, and official AP50 logs enabling exact verification.
